title: Diabetes Basics Explained
summary: This quiz covers the main types, symptoms, diagnosis, and management of diabetes using mainstream medical guidance. It also covers healthy lifestyle habits, monitoring, and prevention of long-term complications.

questions.q: Which of these is a common warning sign of high blood sugar (too much glucose in the blood)?
o: Feeling shaky and sweaty that gets better after eating
Having much more energy and seeing more clearly than usual
Feeling very thirsty and needing to pee often
Having sudden sharp pain in one ankle after a walk
questions.tip: High blood sugar often causes increased thirst and frequent urination as the body tries to remove extra glucose through urine.
questions.eli5: Think of it like a soup that is too salty — your body gets thirsty for water and makes extra pee to help wash the extra sugar away.

questions.q: Which type of diabetes is the most common form in adults?
o: Type 2 diabetes
Type 1 diabetes
Gestational diabetes
Diabetes that only affects newborn babies
questions.tip: Type 2 diabetes is the most common form of diabetes in adults.
questions.eli5: Think of diabetes types like ice cream flavors — vanilla, which is type 2, is ordered far more often by adults than the other flavors.

questions.q: What does prediabetes mean? Prediabetes is when blood sugar is above normal.
o: Blood sugar is much lower than normal and causes fainting
Blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet high enough to be diabetes
The body has stopped making insulin completely
Diabetes that develops only during pregnancy
questions.tip: Prediabetes means blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet in the diabetes range.
questions.eli5: Like a yellow traffic light between green and red, prediabetes is the warning zone before diabetes.

questions.q: What is gestational diabetes?
o: Diabetes that is always present from birth
Damage to the eyes and kidneys after many years of diabetes
Diabetes that can develop during pregnancy
Blood sugar that is higher than normal but below the diabetes range
questions.tip: Gestational diabetes is diabetes that can develop during pregnancy.
questions.eli5: Like a temporary guest staying only for the pregnancy months, this type of diabetes appears during pregnancy.

questions.q: How do symptoms usually differ between type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes?
o: Both types always cause sudden collapse with no early warning
Type 2 symptoms always appear suddenly in a few hours and type 1 takes years
Both types always cause exactly the same speed of symptoms in everyone
Type 1 symptoms usually develop over a short period, while type 2 develops slowly and some people have no symptoms at first
questions.tip: Type 1 symptoms usually develop over a short period, while type 2 develops slowly and some people have no symptoms.
questions.eli5: Like a burst pipe versus a slow drip, type 1 floods in fast while type 2 can leak quietly for a long time.

questions.q: At what age is type 1 diabetes usually first found?
o: Only after age 80 and never earlier
Often in childhood or young adulthood, but it can occur at any age
Only in middle-aged adults who are overweight
Only during pregnancy
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes is often diagnosed in childhood or young adulthood but can occur at any age.
questions.eli5: Like getting freckles, it shows up most in kids and young people, but anyone can get it later too.

questions.q: What basic problem causes diabetes? Insulin is a hormone that helps sugar (glucose) move from the blood into cells.
o: The body makes too much insulin and blood sugar is always too low
The blood has too few red blood cells to carry oxygen
The body does not make enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, so glucose stays in the blood
The stomach cannot digest fruits and vegetables
questions.tip: Diabetes occurs when the body does not make enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, so glucose stays in the blood.
questions.eli5: Like a key that no longer opens the kitchen door, insulin cannot move sugar into cells so sugar piles up in the hallway of the blood.

questions.q: What does prediabetes mean?
o: Blood sugar is normal and insulin is working perfectly
Blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet high enough for diabetes
Blood sugar is already in the diabetes range
Blood sugar is too low because of too much insulin
questions.tip: Prediabetes means blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet in the diabetes range.
questions.eli5: Think like a traffic light turning yellow — not green and not red yet, so it is a warning to slow down.

questions.q: Your A1C test result (average blood sugar over the past 3 months) is 6.0%. What does this usually mean?
o: Low blood sugar
Normal blood sugar
Diabetes
Prediabetes
questions.tip: An HbA1c of 5.7 to 6.4 percent generally indicates prediabetes.
questions.eli5: Like getting a middle grade on a 3-month school report card — not failing, but showing you need to study harder.

questions.q: Why is it important to act on prediabetes?
o: It greatly raises the risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke
It only raises the risk of catching a cold
It means there is no future health risk
It only causes problems during pregnancy
questions.tip: A person with prediabetes is at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes, heart disease, and stroke.
questions.eli5: Like a small crack in a house wall — ignore it and it can lead to much bigger damage later.

questions.q: A fasting blood sugar test (blood sugar after not eating overnight) is 112 mg per dL. Which range is this in?
o: Normal, which is less than 100 mg per dL
Diabetes range, which is 126 mg per dL or higher
Prediabetes range, which is about 100 to 125 mg per dL
Low blood sugar, which is below 70 mg per dL
questions.tip: Normal fasting glucose is less than 100 mg per dL and diabetes is 126 mg per dL or higher, leaving about 100 to 125 mg per dL as the prediabetes range.
questions.eli5: Like water warming on the stove — not cold and not yet boiling, sitting in the middle warm zone.

questions.q: Which habit is proven to greatly lower the chance that prediabetes turns into type 2 diabetes?
o: Skipping meals for several days to drop weight quickly
Losing about 5 to 7 percent of body weight with about 30 minutes of daily activity
Eating mostly processed snacks and sitting most of the day
Stopping all fruits, vegetables, and whole grains
questions.tip: Losing 5 to 7 percent of body weight with about 30 minutes of daily exercise reduced diabetes risk by more than half in a major study.
questions.eli5: Like tidying a messy kitchen a little every day — small steady effort keeps the big mess from happening.

questions.q: Which statement about symptoms in prediabetes is most accurate?
o: It always causes severe thirst and frequent urination
It always causes rapid weight loss within days
It always causes seizures and vision changes
It often causes no symptoms, so a blood test is needed to find it
questions.tip: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes develop slowly and often cause no symptoms at all.
questions.eli5: Like homework piling up quietly in a backpack — you may not notice until a teacher checks it.

questions.q: Which two changes in hunger and thirst are common symptoms of diabetes?
o: Decreased hunger and decreased thirst
Increased hunger and increased thirst
Increased hunger but much less thirst
Decreased hunger but much more thirst
questions.tip: General symptoms of diabetes include both increased hunger and increased thirst.
questions.eli5: Like a car that cannot use its fuel, the body keeps asking for more food and water.

questions.q: When blood sugar stays high, why do frequent urination and constant thirst often happen together?
o: High blood sugar makes the body hold onto water, so you urinate less and feel less thirsty
High blood sugar mainly affects the joints, so thirst and urination stay normal
High blood sugar lowers the desire for fluids, so you drink less and urinate less
High blood sugar makes the kidneys pass extra water as urine, and that fluid loss makes you thirsty
questions.tip: Frequent urination and persistent thirst are common symptoms of high blood sugar.
questions.eli5: Like overfilling a cup so it spills over, extra sugar pulls extra water out and you feel thirsty to refill it.

questions.q: Which of these everyday feelings can be early signs of diabetes?
o: Feeling very tired a lot and having a dry mouth
Feeling full of energy and never feeling thirsty
Having sharper hearing and sleeping less at night
Having stronger muscles and a very moist mouth
questions.tip: Feeling very tired and having a dry mouth can be early signs of diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like a phone that will not charge, the cells lack usable energy so you feel worn out and dry.

questions.q: Which change in eyesight can be an early sign of high blood sugar?
o: Night vision becomes much sharper than normal
Colors look brighter and never fade
Vision becomes blurry, like looking through fog
Side vision becomes much wider than normal
questions.tip: Having blurry vision can be an early sign of diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like looking through a steamy bathroom mirror after a shower, things look fuzzy and unclear.

questions.q: A small cut on the foot stays open for many weeks in a person with high blood sugar. What does this suggest?
o: Cuts healing much faster than usual is typical with high blood sugar
Sores that take a long time to heal can occur with high blood sugar
High blood sugar prevents cuts from happening at all
High blood sugar only changes skin color and does not affect healing
questions.tip: Sores that take a long time to heal can occur when blood sugar stays high.
questions.eli5: Like a road repair slowed by bad weather, the body fixes skin more slowly when sugar stays high.

questions.q: Which nerve-related feeling in the hands or feet is more commonly noted with type 2 diabetes over time?
o: Sharp joint pain that happens only after heavy lifting
Itchy skin that clears up after one shower
Muscle cramps that happen only during exercise
Tingling or numbness in the hands or feet
questions.tip: Tingling in the hands or feet is more commonly noted with type 2 diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like a foot falling asleep after sitting too long in school, irritated nerves can tingle or feel numb.

questions.q: What causes type 1 diabetes?
o: Eating too much sugar in one week suddenly stops insulin production
The body's immune system destroys the pancreas cells that make insulin
The kidneys lose the ability to remove extra sugar from the blood
The stomach stops digesting carbohydrates into glucose
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes happens when an autoimmune attack destroys insulin-making beta cells, so little or no insulin is made.
questions.eli5: Like a bakery losing all its bakers, so no bread — or in this case insulin — can be made.

questions.q: What mainly causes high blood sugar in type 2 diabetes?
o: The body responds poorly to insulin and over time cannot make enough insulin to keep blood sugar normal
The body makes insulin that works too well and pulls too much sugar into cells
The immune system destroys all insulin-making cells within a few days in adulthood
The lungs cannot carry enough oxygen, so sugar builds up in the blood
questions.tip: Type 2 diabetes involves insulin resistance plus a gradual failure to make enough insulin, so glucose stays in the blood.
questions.eli5: Like a rusty lock and a tired key-maker — the keys do not turn well and fewer keys are made.

questions.q: Which combination most raises a person's risk of developing type 2 diabetes?
o: Young age, normal weight, and daily exercise
Balanced meals with vegetables, whole grains, and lean protein
Drinking plenty of water and sleeping 7 to 8 hours a night
Carrying extra body weight, being inactive, and having a family history of diabetes
questions.tip: Overweight, physical inactivity, and family history are major risk factors for type 2 diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like carrying a heavy backpack uphill every day — extra strain makes the body's sugar system wear out faster.

questions.q: How do carrying extra body weight and getting little exercise increase the risk of type 2 diabetes?
o: They cause the pancreas to make far too much insulin that works too fast
They make the kidneys filter blood sugar too quickly
They make the body's cells respond poorly to insulin, so sugar stays in the blood
They cause the immune system to destroy all insulin in a few days
questions.tip: Excess weight and inactivity promote insulin resistance, where cells do not use insulin properly.
questions.eli5: Like shouting through a thick closed door — the message from insulin does not get through, so sugar piles up outside.

questions.q: Which 2 of these are known risk factors for type 2 diabetes? (Choose 2)
o: Having had gestational diabetes during pregnancy
Drinking water instead of sugary soda every day
Having a parent or sibling with type 2 diabetes
Staying at a healthy weight with regular exercise
questions.tip: History of gestational diabetes and family history both raise future risk of type 2 diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like family recipes and past kitchen troubles — what runs in the family and what happened in pregnancy can hint at future trouble.

questions.q: A woman had gestational diabetes (high blood sugar during pregnancy) that went away after birth. What is true about her future risk?
o: She has no higher future risk than someone who never had it
She will definitely develop type 1 diabetes within a year
Her child is guaranteed never to get diabetes
She has a higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes later and needs follow-up checks
questions.tip: A history of gestational diabetes greatly raises later risk of type 2 diabetes for the mother.
questions.eli5: Like a smoke alarm that went off once — even if quiet now, you watch more closely for fire later.

questions.q: What does the A1C (HbA1c) blood test measure?
o: The blood sugar level at the exact minute of the test
The level of cholesterol in the blood
The average blood sugar level over the past 3 months
The amount of insulin made after one meal
questions.tip: The A1C test measures average blood sugar levels over the past 3 months.
questions.eli5: Like a report card average for the whole term, not just one quiz, A1C shows how blood sugar did over months.

questions.q: Which HbA1c level generally indicates diabetes?
o: Below 5.7 percent
5.0 percent
6.0 percent
6.5 percent or higher
questions.tip: An HbA1c of 6.5 percent or higher generally indicates diabetes.
questions.eli5: Think of 6.5 as a line on a measuring wall — at or above that line means diabetes range.

questions.q: What is considered a normal fasting plasma glucose level (blood sugar after not eating overnight)?
o: Less than 100 mg per dL
100 to 125 mg per dL
126 mg per dL or higher
200 mg per dL or higher
questions.tip: Normal fasting plasma glucose is less than 100 mg per dL.
questions.eli5: Like an empty shopping cart before the store opens, morning blood sugar should start low, under 100.

questions.q: A person has a fasting blood sugar of 132 mg per dL, and a repeat test on another day is also above 126 mg per dL. What does this usually suggest?
o: A normal fasting level
Diabetes when confirmed by repeat testing
Low blood sugar from skipping meals
Prediabetes range only
questions.tip: A fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg per dL or higher can indicate diabetes when confirmed by repeat testing.
questions.eli5: Like needing two photos to prove a tall plant, doctors use two high morning readings to confirm diabetes.

questions.q: Why can type 2 diabetes go unnoticed for a long time before diagnosis?
o: It develops slowly and some people with high blood sugar have no symptoms
Symptoms of type 2 always develop very quickly over a few hours
High blood sugar in type 2 always causes a fever that is easy to notice
Blood tests cannot show high blood sugar in type 2
questions.tip: Type 2 diabetes develops slowly and some people with high blood sugar have no symptoms at all.
questions.eli5: Like a slow leak in a bike tire, type 2 can build up quietly without you feeling it at first.

questions.q: Which set of information can doctors use together to diagnose diabetes?
o: Blood pressure reading alone
Fasting glucose, symptoms, glucose tolerance testing, and HbA1c levels
Cholesterol result alone
Body weight on one day alone
questions.tip: Diagnosis of diabetes can involve fasting glucose, symptoms, glucose tolerance testing, and HbA1c levels.
questions.eli5: Like using pieces of a puzzle, doctors put blood tests plus symptoms together to see the full picture.

questions.q: What does an HbA1c test (A1C test for average blood sugar) mainly tell you?
o: It shows blood sugar only at the exact minute of the blood draw.
It shows the average blood sugar level over about the past 3 months.
It shows how much food was eaten on the day of the test.
It shows blood pressure and cholesterol levels over the past year.
questions.tip: The A1C test measures average blood sugar levels over the past 3 months.
questions.eli5: Think of it like a movie of the last 3 months, not a single photo from today.

questions.q: An adult has an HbA1c test result of 5.3% (a test of average blood sugar). How is this result usually described?
o: Diabetes, because it is above the diabetes level
Prediabetes, because it is between 5.7% and 6.4%
Low blood sugar that needs emergency sugar
Normal, because it is below 5.7%
questions.tip: A normal HbA1c level is below 5.7 percent.
questions.eli5: Like staying under a speed limit — 5.3 is still in the safe zone under 5.7.

questions.q: A person has an HbA1c (average blood sugar test) of 7.2% on two separate lab tests. What does this usually mean?
o: Diabetes, because 6.5% or higher generally indicates diabetes
Normal blood sugar, because it is below 5.7%
Prediabetes, because it is between 5.7% and 6.4%
Low blood sugar from too little glucose in the blood
questions.tip: An HbA1c of 6.5 percent or higher generally indicates diabetes.
questions.eli5: Like a fever thermometer with a clear line — once you cross 6.5, you are in the diabetes range.

questions.q: Why does a doctor order an HbA1c test (average blood sugar test) every 3 to 6 months for someone with diabetes?
o: To replace daily glucose checks because daily checks are no longer needed
To see how one single meal affected blood sugar that morning
To check long-term average control and help adjust the care plan
To measure blood pressure and cholesterol instead of blood sugar
questions.tip: The A1C test is commonly used to help manage diabetes and guide treatment over time.
questions.eli5: Like a coach looking at the whole season average to decide if practice needs to change.

questions.q: Which HbA1c (average blood sugar) range generally indicates prediabetes (blood sugar higher than normal but not yet diabetes)?
o: Below 4.0%
Below 5.7%
Above 8.0% only
From 5.7% to 6.4%
questions.tip: An HbA1c from 5.7 percent to 6.4 percent generally indicates prediabetes.
questions.eli5: Like a yellow traffic light between green and red — a warning to slow down before diabetes.

questions.q: Which 2 test results generally point to diabetes when confirmed by repeat testing? (Choose 2)
o: HbA1c of 6.5% or higher
Fasting blood sugar (after not eating overnight) of 126 mg per dL or higher
Fasting blood sugar (after not eating overnight) of 85 mg per dL
HbA1c of 5.0%
questions.tip: Diabetes is generally indicated by HbA1c of 6.5% or higher or fasting glucose of 126 mg per dL or higher when confirmed.
questions.eli5: Think of them as two different alarms — if either alarm rings twice, sugar is staying too high.

questions.q: Why do many people with diabetes check their blood sugar at home each day with a meter (finger-stick test)?
o: To cure diabetes after a few normal readings
To see how food, activity, and medicine affect sugar that day so care can be adjusted
To replace the need for an A1C lab test forever
To measure blood pressure and cholesterol at the same time
questions.tip: Daily glucose monitoring shows day-to-day patterns so food, activity, and medicine can be adjusted.
questions.eli5: Like checking the weather before you dress, a daily sugar check tells you what is happening right now.

questions.q: How is a home finger-stick sugar reading different from an A1C lab test?
o: A finger-stick shows sugar at that moment, while A1C shows the average over about 3 months
A finger-stick shows the 3-month average, while A1C shows sugar at that moment
A finger-stick measures cholesterol, while A1C measures blood pressure
There is no difference; they measure exactly the same time period
questions.tip: A home meter measures glucose at one moment, while A1C reflects average glucose over about 3 months.
questions.eli5: A finger-stick is like one photo, while A1C is like a whole season of photos put together.

questions.q: A person who takes insulin checks sugar often because low blood sugar can be dangerous. Which signs may mean severe low blood sugar that needs quick help?
o: A slow-healing sore and constant thirst
Dry mouth and needing to urinate often
Gradual weight gain over many months
Confusion, shakiness, vision changes, or seizure
questions.tip: Severe low blood sugar with insulin use may cause disorientation, vision changes, shakiness, and seizures.
questions.eli5: Think of the brain like a phone needing charge; when sugar drops too low, the screen glitches and may shut down.

questions.q: Which 2 are part of current diabetes care along with healthy eating and regular activity? (Choose 2)
o: Skipping meals whenever sugar looks high
Checking blood sugar as advised and tracking the results
Taking diabetes medicine as prescribed and having A1C checked as advised
Stopping checkups once you feel fine for a few days
questions.tip: Current management can include diet, exercise, medication, daily glucose monitoring, and HbA1c monitoring.
questions.eli5: Like caring for a garden with water plus weeding and checking the soil, diabetes care uses several tools together.

questions.q: If home meter readings and lab tests stay high for many weeks, why do doctors worry even if the person still feels okay?
o: High sugar for one hour always causes instant blindness
High readings mean the meter is broken and should be thrown away
Continuing high glucose can damage blood vessels and nerves over time, raising risk of heart, eye, kidney, nerve, and foot problems
High readings only cause hunger and have no long-term effects
questions.tip: Continuing high blood glucose can damage blood vessels and nerves over time.
questions.eli5: Like a slow leak rusting pipes, high sugar quietly harms vessels and nerves over months and years.

questions.q: What is a good way to use home blood sugar results at clinic visits?
o: Check only once a year and ignore daily patterns
Bring a dated log of readings with notes on meals, activity, and medicine so the care team can spot patterns
Throw the numbers away and try to remember one good reading
Share only low readings and hide high readings
questions.tip: Keeping and sharing a log of glucose results helps the care team find patterns and adjust the care plan.
questions.eli5: Like bringing a homework notebook to show your work, a sugar log helps the team see the full story, not just one page.

questions.q: Where in the body is insulin (the hormone that controls blood sugar) normally made?
o: In the liver
In the kidneys
In the pancreas
In the lungs
questions.tip: Insulin is normally made by beta cells in the pancreas.
questions.eli5: Think of the pancreas as a small kitchen behind the stomach that cooks up insulin when needed.

questions.q: In a person without diabetes, when does the body normally release more insulin?
o: Right after eating, when blood sugar rises
Only during deep sleep at night
Only when a person feels very thirsty
When blood sugar is already very low
questions.tip: Rising blood sugar after a meal normally triggers the pancreas to release more insulin.
questions.eli5: Like turning on a fan when a room gets hot, the body sends out more insulin when sugar in the blood goes up after food.

questions.q: What does insulin resistance (a key problem in type 2 diabetes) mean?
o: The body is allergic to sugar and gets a skin rash
The pancreas makes extra juices to digest fatty foods
The immune system destroys all insulin within minutes
The body's cells respond poorly to insulin, so glucose stays in the blood
questions.tip: Insulin resistance means cells do not respond well to insulin, so glucose remains in the blood.
questions.eli5: It is like a rusty lock that will not turn well even with the right key, so the door into cells stays shut.

questions.q: How does the insulin problem in type 1 diabetes mainly differ from the problem in type 2 diabetes?
o: In type 1 the body makes too much insulin; in type 2 the body makes none at all
In type 1 the body makes little or no insulin; in type 2 the body does not use insulin well
In type 1 insulin raises body temperature; in type 2 insulin lowers body temperature
In type 1 exercise replaces insulin; in type 2 diet replaces insulin
questions.tip: Type 1 diabetes mainly involves little or no insulin production, while type 2 mainly involves poor use of insulin.
questions.eli5: Type 1 is like a factory that closed down and makes nothing, while type 2 is like workers ignoring the delivery truck.

questions.q: After insulin helps sugar (glucose) enter cells, what does insulin also help the body do with extra sugar?
o: Turn extra sugar directly into water to be breathed out
Send extra sugar to the lungs to help breathing
Store extra sugar in the liver and muscles for later energy
Change extra sugar into salt for the kidneys to keep
questions.tip: Insulin helps cells use glucose for energy now and helps store extra glucose in liver and muscle for later.
questions.eli5: Like packing leftovers into lunchboxes for tomorrow, insulin helps save extra sugar for when you need energy later.

questions.q: A person who uses insulin becomes confused, has vision changes, and in a severe case has a seizure. What does this suggest?
o: Blood sugar has dropped too low from too much insulin effect
A common cold with no link to blood sugar
Healthy digestion after a balanced meal
Extra vitamins from food building up in the blood
questions.tip: Too much insulin effect can cause severe low blood sugar, which may cause confusion, vision changes, and seizures.
questions.eli5: Too much insulin is like pressing the brakes too hard on a car, dropping blood sugar so low the brain cannot steer clearly.

questions.q: Which group of people must take insulin (blood-sugar-lowering hormone medicine) every day to stay alive?
o: Adults with prediabetes, because their blood sugar is slightly above normal
People with type 1 diabetes, because their body makes little or no insulin
People with type 2 diabetes whose blood sugar is controlled by diet and exercise alone
Women who had gestational diabetes in the past but now have normal blood sugar
questions.tip: People with type 1 diabetes make little or no insulin, so they need daily insulin to live.
questions.eli5: It is like a kitchen with no stove — you have to bring in heat from outside to cook the food.

questions.q: Metformin is a common first-choice pill for type 2 diabetes. What is its main job when used with healthy eating and activity?
o: Replace insulin in people with type 1 diabetes
Raise blood sugar quickly during low blood sugar
Cure diabetes so medicine can be stopped after a few days
Help lower blood sugar, partly by reducing sugar made by the liver and helping the body use insulin better
questions.tip: Metformin is commonly used in type 2 diabetes to help lower blood sugar along with diet and exercise.
questions.eli5: Think of the liver as a sugar faucet left dripping — metformin helps turn that extra drip down.

questions.q: Why is insulin usually given as a shot, insulin pen, or pump instead of being swallowed as a regular pill?
o: Stomach acids and digestion would break down insulin before it could work
Shots work only on the skin and never reach the blood
Pills always work faster than shots for all hormones
Insulin would permanently damage the stomach if swallowed
questions.tip: Insulin is a protein hormone that digestion would destroy, so it must go directly into the body by shot or pump.
questions.eli5: It is like an ice sculpture sent through a hot oven — it would melt before it arrived.

questions.q: A person takes insulin or another diabetes medicine that lowers blood sugar. Which safety habit is most important to prevent dangerously low blood sugar?
o: Skip meals when busy and take the same dose to save time
Take an extra dose whenever feeling tired without checking sugar
Take medicine as prescribed, eat meals regularly, and check blood sugar as advised
Stop checking blood sugar once you feel okay for a few days
questions.tip: Insulin and some diabetes medicines can cause low blood sugar, so regular meals and monitoring as advised are key safety steps.
questions.eli5: It is like balancing water in a bucket — medicine lets water out, and regular meals keep refilling it so it does not run empty.

questions.q: A person with type 2 diabetes starts taking diabetes medicine and blood sugar improves. What is true about diet and exercise after starting medicine?
o: Healthy eating and activity are no longer needed once medicine is started
Healthy eating and activity are still needed because they work together with medicine
Exercise should be stopped because medicine does all the work
Diet only matters for type 1 diabetes, not when taking type 2 pills
questions.tip: Current diabetes care combines medicine with healthy eating and regular activity, not medicine alone.
questions.eli5: Medicine and healthy habits are like two oars on a boat — you need both rowing together to move straight.

questions.q: Why do many people with diabetes also take medicines for blood pressure and cholesterol, even when blood sugar is improving?
o: To help lower the risk of heart, kidney, and vessel problems linked to diabetes
To raise blood sugar to a normal level
To replace the need for blood sugar checks and A1C tests
To cure type 1 diabetes so insulin is no longer needed
questions.tip: Managing blood pressure and cholesterol lowers the risk of heart and kidney complications in diabetes.
questions.eli5: High sugar harms pipes over time, like rust in plumbing — protecting pressure and cholesterol helps keep the pipes safe.

questions.q: Which eating pattern best helps prevent type 2 diabetes and keep blood sugar steady?
o: Mostly fried foods, sweets, and sugary drinks with little vegetables
Mostly vegetables, fruits, whole grains, beans, and lean proteins like fish or chicken
Skipping meals and then eating one very large meal late at night
Eating only meat and butter while avoiding all fruits and whole grains
questions.tip: A balanced pattern rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and lean proteins helps prevent type 2 diabetes.
questions.eli5: Think of your body like a car engine — clean, steady fuel like veggies and whole grains keeps it running smooth, not sputtering.

questions.q: Why are regular soda and sweetened fruit drinks a poor choice for blood sugar control?
o: They contain a lot of added sugar that raises blood sugar quickly with little nutrition
They contain too much fiber that blocks all sugar from being used
They contain too much protein that raises blood sugar for many hours
They have no calories so they cause low blood sugar right away
questions.tip: Sugary drinks provide large amounts of fast-absorbing added sugar that spikes blood glucose.
questions.eli5: Sugary drinks are like dumping a bucket of water on a fire at once — a fast flood of sugar hits the blood, like a rush in a checkout line.

questions.q: Why are whole grains like oats, brown rice, and whole wheat often a better choice than white bread and white rice?
o: White bread has more fiber and vitamins than whole grains
Whole grains and white grains affect blood sugar in exactly the same way
Whole grains cost less sugar to make so they taste sweeter
Whole grains have more fiber, which slows digestion and causes a slower rise in blood sugar
questions.tip: Fiber in whole grains slows digestion and leads to a slower, steadier rise in blood sugar than refined grains.
questions.eli5: Think of fiber like speed bumps on a road — whole-grain foods slow the sugar traffic so it does not all rush in at once.

questions.q: What is the diabetes plate method for building a balanced meal?
o: Fill the whole plate with meat and add sugary sauce on top
Fill half the plate with fruit juice, one quarter with candy, and one quarter with white bread
Fill half the plate with non-starchy vegetables, one quarter with lean protein, and one quarter with whole grains or starchy vegetables
Skip vegetables and protein and fill the whole plate with large portions of pasta or rice
questions.tip: The plate method is about half non-starchy vegetables, one-quarter lean protein, and one-quarter whole grains or starchy foods.
questions.eli5: Picture your plate like a school lunch tray divided into sections — veggies get the biggest spot, like the main playground, with smaller spots for protein and grains.

questions.q: Which fat choice fits a diabetes-friendly, heart-healthy eating pattern?
o: Cooking often with butter, lard, and fatty processed meats
Using liquid plant oils like olive or canola oil, plus nuts and fish, instead of solid animal fats
Avoiding all fats and eating mostly sweets and sugary snacks instead
Eating deep-fried foods and pastries every day for energy
questions.tip: Unsaturated fats from plant oils, nuts, and fish are healthier for heart and blood vessels than saturated fats from butter and fatty meats.
questions.eli5: Think of pipes in a kitchen sink — liquid plant oils and fish fats are like warm soapy water that keeps pipes clearer than thick grease from butter.

questions.q: Why is eating regular meals with steady portions of carbohydrate foods (bread, rice, pasta, fruit) helpful for blood sugar?
